Interesting but their whole attempt at building a common language is seems flawed. Starting with writing 'Human' on a board just isn't right.

Your best bet is probably to assume the aliens are logically intelligent with some level of mathematical understanding. Then start with counting. Assuming visual communication you can start with dots. 

o
o o
o o o
o o o o
etc

Then introduce operators like equals, not equals, addition, multiplication, etc. 

o = o
o + o = o o
o + o o = o o o
o o + o = o o o
o * o = o
o * o o = o o 
o o * o o = o o o o
o != o o
o o != o
etc

You can use to introduce the concept of true or false (yes or no). 

T : o = o
F : o = o o

You can also start symbol subsitution 

o = 1
o o = 2
o o o = 3
1 + 1 = o + o = o o = 2
etc

From this you can basically define an entire basic logic (less than, greater than, implication, etc...). You can also start introducing slightly more abstract concepts like geometry and set theory, and start introducing concepts like time and distance and whatever.

From there you can start moving into more linguistic constructions.

This is basis of the Lincos artificial language which was proposed as a starting point for communicating with extraterrestrials.

This of course only works if the extraterrestrials understand mathematical concepts. It could be they are purely instinctial or use a logic framework wholely incompatible with anything we can concieve of. But I think it's a better approach than blindly dropping a human linguistics expert in front of an alien. As different as human languages and societies can be we still tend to share basic thought processes such as concept serialization which makes finding common ground between human languages so much easier. It is quite possible an alien processes their environment in a completely non-linear way would make standard human linguistic approaches pretty much useless.
